name: vLLM's request logger writes full prompt bodies and token ids into the application log stream at DEBUG, with no field-level redaction anywhere in the engine
symptom: A deployment is found to have retained a year of prompt text and token ids in its log aggregator. Nobody enabled PII capture: --enable-log-requests plus a DEBUG log level does it, and the engine offers truncation (--max-log-len) but no redaction and no field selection.
root_cause: RequestLogger.log_inputs() emits the raw prompt string via %r at DEBUG together with prompt_token_ids unredacted, and log_request_body() dumps request.model_dump_json(exclude_unset=True) at DEBUG. The engine-args doc makes the level dependency explicit: at INFO you get request id, parameters and LoRA request; the PROMPT TEXT AND TOKEN IDS require --log-level DEBUG. --max-log-len truncates and there is no counterpart flag for redaction. This is the concrete mechanism behind every compliance problem in this slice: the operational observability setting people actually turn on to debug a serving deployment is the same setting that writes user content to disk.
workaround: Never run a serving node containing regulated or personal data at DEBUG log level in production, and treat any log level above INFO as a privacy control rather than a verbosity choice. Where prompt-level debugging is required, capture to an access-controlled store with a defined TTL and a documented legal basis, not to the general log pipeline. If you need per-request correlation for audit, use the request ID, which is logged at INFO - that is sufficient for an audit trail without retaining content.
notes: The INFO-versus-DEBUG distinction is the single most useful operational fact here and it is easy to miss because the flag is named --enable-log-requests, which sounds like it enables request logging generally. It does not enable prompt content at INFO. Correlating audit events does NOT require prompt bodies: the request ID is logged at INFO. SCHEME RECLASSIFIED (2026-10-04): was 'config'. Filed as privacy rather than security: the subject is prompt content (and token ids) written unredacted into the log stream - a content-leakage-in-logs record, not an attack-surface one.
